title.narrative: Tripartite partners in Suriname, based on an enabling environmental assessment, have developed national frameworks or policies for the creation of an environment conducive to sustainable enterprises

description.narrative:
Suriname, despite its vast forest coverage, relies heavily on natural resources like gold, timber, oil, and gas. The country aims to diversify its economy through the Multi-Year Development Plan 2022-2026, which aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and promotes sustainable tourism and agriculture. However, Suriname faces structural challenges, including a large informal economy, high public sector employment, and difficulties in starting businesses. Suriname's Third Decent Work Country Program (DWCP) 2023-2026 addresses these issues by promoting decentralized sector development and creating a participative platform involving indigenous populations.
ILO provides technical assistance on "Promoting just transition" and "Addressing informality," aiming to increase policy formulation capacity by a stronger understanding of the topics and an evidence based social dialogue, transition enterprises to formality and greening of their businesses, and enable a just transition in local territories by improved access to information and planning. For this initiative the ILO is working with multiple stakeholders such as the Ministry of Labour, the Ministry of Environment, employers, workers and government officials at national, district and local level. The initiative will benefit Surinamese enterprises, local governments, and community leaders by fostering economic diversification, sustainable enterprise development, and decent job creation.
